fix(native-file): prevent crash when unlinking missing files

NativeFileSpec.unlink is codegened as a void-returning TurboModule
method, which dispatches asynchronously on the mqt_v_native thread.
Throwing "File does not exist" there bypasses every JS try/catch and
surfaces as a fatal AndroidRuntime exception, killing the process.

does not exist. The Downloads "delete all" and individual delete
flows previously crashed whenever a chapter row had isDownloaded=true
while its on-disk folder had already been removed (e.g. after backup
restore or external cleanup). The same fix also protects useNovel,
pluginManager, fetch, epub/import, backup/local, backup/utils, and
AdvancedTab call sites that share the same native handler.

[skip ci]

* perf(reader): Cut Chapter Open Latency and Reading-Time Re-Renders

Opening a chapter blocked the first paint on work that is not needed to
show text, and mounted several heavy subtrees while that work was running.

Load path (useChapter):
- Render the chapter as soon as its text is ready. Resolving the next and
  previous chapter (two full-scan queries, plus a plugin page fetch over
  the network at a page boundary) now runs after the chapter is on screen
  and is pushed into the WebView instead of being baked into its HTML.
- Read downloaded chapters with a single native call instead of
  exists() + readFile(), and start that read in parallel with the
  database lookup instead of after it.
- Cache render-ready (sanitized) HTML, so prefetched chapters skip
  sanitize-html entirely, and prefetch when the JS thread is idle rather
  than in the middle of the current load.
- Drop failed loads from the cache so a retry actually retries.
- Guard every load with a generation id, keep getChapter and friends
  referentially stable, and defer history/last-read writes off the
  critical path.

Mounting:
- The chapter drawer (a list of every chapter) and the settings sheet
  (a tab view that enumerates TTS engines and voices) are mounted on
  first use instead of at reader open; the sheet's tabs are lazy.
- The loading skeleton shimmers its first lines only instead of
  animating a full screen of gradient views.

While reading:
- Progress and mark-as-read writes keep the chapter array identity when
  nothing changed, and a chapter is marked read (and pushed to the
  tracker) once instead of on every progress report.
- Drawer rows are a memoized component with stable props, the drawer
  stylesheet is memoized, and the WebView document is built once per
  chapter instead of on every reader re-render.

Also fixes the drawer's loading branch, which compared a ref object to
undefined and was therefore unreachable, and guards page-reader
transitions against a not-yet-resolved neighbour.

* perf(reader): Stop Double-Parsing the Chapter and Cut Per-Frame Work

Follow-up to the previous pass, mostly inside the reader document itself.

Chapter open:
- The chapter body was written back into the DOM on every open. The
  document already arrives with the chapter parsed, so unless bionic
  reading or paragraph-spacing removal is on, that re-parsed and
  re-laid-out the whole chapter (and restarted image loads) for nothing.
  It now only writes when the transformed markup actually differs.
- The reading position was restored from `window.load` via
  `document.fonts.ready`, both of which wait for every image in the
  chapter - measured at ~1.5s with a single slow image, during which the
  reader sat at the top of the chapter. It is now restored once the
  chapter is parsed and styled (~100ms in the same scenario) with an
  instant scroll, and corrected afterwards if fonts or images changed the
  height - but only while the reader is still where it was put, so it
  cannot yank the page from under someone already reading.

While reading:
- The scrollbar and the footer percentage each had their own unthrottled
  scroll listener recomputing the same ratio; they now share one
  listener coalesced to a frame. The footer clock no longer ticks state
  when the footer is hidden.
- Reading time is persisted without rebuilding the in-memory chapter
  list. It was rebuilt every few seconds for a field no screen renders -
  the statistics screen aggregates it from the database - and on Fabric
  react-navigation deliberately does not freeze the screen below the
  focused one, so it re-rendered the novel screen's chapter list too.
- `hidden` moved into its own context. It flips on every tap on the page,
  and a context value change re-renders all consumers, so the WebView,
  drawer, appbar and searchbar were all re-rendering for a flag only the
  reader screen reads.
- `openPage` no longer re-queries the chapter list when the requested
  page is already open, which the drawer does on every mount.

Smaller: the battery level is read asynchronously instead of through two
synchronous native calls per chapter, the sanitizer options object is
built once instead of per chapter, the general settings tab draws its
dozen fixed rows directly instead of virtualising them, and the reader
settings hook stops allocating a new settings object per render.

Verified the document changes by loading the real reader assets in
Chromium: position restored before load, no body rewrite when no
transform applies, both scroll indicators driven by the shared listener,
progress still reported, transforms still applied and reverted, and the
post-load correction only firing on an untouched reader.

fix: Remove White Flash During Screen Transitions (Closes #1926) (#1927)

`AppTheme` never set `android:windowBackground`, so it was inherited from
`Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar` and resolved to a near-white colour
whenever the system was in light mode — independently of the theme picked
inside the app. Nothing between that window and the navigators painted a
background of its own: the root view, `GestureHandlerRootView` and
`SafeAreaProvider` are all transparent, and only the individual screens carry
`contentStyle`. Any frame in which no screen was drawn — mounting a nested
navigator such as `MoreStack` or `ReaderStack`, or freezing the screen being
left — therefore showed the white window through.

Paint the root view with the active theme background so the window stays
covered, and give `AppTheme` a day/night `android:windowBackground` so the
frames before React draws are themed as well. The chapter screen additionally
uses the reader background instead of the app background, so pushing it no
longer flashes the app theme before the reader appears.

fix: Stop Bottom Nav Icons Trembling On Tab Press (Closes #2041) (#2047)

The focused tab indicator animated `width` directly, which triggered layout every frame — Yoga's per-node pixel rounding then shifted the icon and label inconsistently as the width swept through fractional values, causing a visible tremble. Fixed by giving the icon a fixed-size box and animating the indicator via `scaleX` on an absolutely positioned sibling instead, since transforms don't trigger layout.

fix: Prevent Chapter Drawer Blank Flash On Open (Closes #2038) (#2048)

Opening the reader's chapter drawer flashed an empty panel before the
chapter list appeared, most visibly on slower devices.

Three things combined to cause it:

- The panel carried `backgroundColor: 'transparent'`, which overrode the
  opaque default `react-native-drawer-layout` applies to its own
  `styles.drawer`. Since `drawerStyle` is applied last in the panel's
  style array, the panel had no background at all, so the reader showed
  through it for every frame before the content painted. It now carries
  the drawer's own `theme.surface`, matching what the content already
  paints, so the panel is opaque from the first frame.

- The chapter list was mounted by the same handler that opened the
  drawer, so the slide-in animation (UI thread) ran while the list was
  still mounting and measuring (JS thread). The list is now mounted once
  the chapter has loaded and interactions have settled, before the
  drawer is first opened. A closed panel stays laid out -- it is only
  translated off-screen -- so the list measures and renders its first
  rows out of sight instead of during the animation.

- When the list mounted after the chapters arrived, it was scrolled to
  the current chapter with an animation even though `initialScrollIndex`
  had already placed it there, adding a second visible jump. That scroll
  is now skipped on the initial mount and kept for later chapter
  changes.
